summary: An excerpt from a novel (labeled Book 11, part 55) about Rebecca, a child whose self-punishing sacrifices go awry. She misses the Sunday-school concert, which leaves two infants unprompted and classmates unready for a difficult scripture reading. Resolving to give up her dearest possession, she throws her beloved pink parasol down the well, feeling righteous. The next morning the parasol's ivory hook snags the well's chain gear, and Abijah Flagg retrieves it from the well after the family has trouble drawing water.
one_line: Rebecca throws her beloved pink parasol down the well as self-punishment, only to have it jam the well's chain gear.
key_facts: Rebecca stayed home from the Sunday-school concert, which she was extremely fond of, as her first experimental attempt at martyrdom.
Two infants who relied on Rebecca to prompt them broke down ignominiously at the Sunday-school concert because of her absence.
The class had to read a difficult chapter of Scripture in rotation, and the blow descended when the Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Perizzites had to be pronounced.
Rebecca decided to give up her beloved pink parasol as her act of self-punishment.
Rebecca feared she lacked the moral energy to break the pink parasol into bits, so she decided to fling it into the well.
Rebecca threw the parasol down the well at night, having slipped out the front door and lifted the well cover.
Rebecca compared herself to heathen mothers who cast their babes to the crocodiles in the Ganges, which helped her at the crucial moment of renunciation.
Rebecca slept well and arose refreshed, then went to school after breakfast.
After breakfast there was great difficulty in drawing water from the well.
Abijah Flagg was summoned, lifted the well cover, explored, and found the cause of the trouble.
The ivory hook of the parasol had caught in the chain gear of the well.
When water was first drawn, the parasol was jerked up, bent, and its strong ribs jammed into the well side, becoming entangled.
Abijah Flagg removed the parasol from the well with the help of Yankee wit.
